A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DuoduoCLIP and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Shared content can be reliably matched despite added appendix sections, redrawn figures, and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original classification and retrieval results, efficiency measurements, and ablations in the main text and Appendix A.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds initialization experiments, baseline evaluations, and qualitative retrieval demonstrations.

M1.justification: The default encoder, cross-view attention, embedding averaging, and training losses remain unchanged. Appendix A.4.2 adds a limited inference extension for concept mixing: retrieve an existing object by maximizing its minimum similarity to two input shape embeddings.

E1.justification: V3 adds retrieval from manually cropped web and Stable Diffusion 3 scene images, plus two-object concept-mixing retrieval on Objaverse (Appendix A.4). Existing training datasets and quantitative benchmark coverage are retained.

E2.justification: V3 adds MixCon3D to Table 2 and FT B-32 to Tables 2–4. The single-view training control underlying FT B-32 already appeared in v2's Table 9, but its participation in these classification and text-retrieval comparisons is new.

E3.justification: Existing splits, metrics, and default training settings remain unchanged. New experiments compare OpenAI versus OpenCLIP initialization, with an additional linear layer for the OpenAI variant, and specify single-view scene queries against a database encoded with 12 views per object (Appendices A.2.3 and A.4.1).

E4.justification: Appendix A.2.3 adds an ablation testing whether the shape encoder and frozen CLIP encoders need matching initialization. Appendix A.4 adds qualitative distribution-shift and concept-mixing case studies. Existing view-count, layer-count, attention, MLP, and camera-sampling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that evaluations are averaged over three different seeds in Section 4.2.1. V3 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Shared numerical table entries remain unchanged. New entries include FT B-32 retrieval scores of 15.01/32.46 RR@1/RR@5, MixCon3D comparisons, and initialization results: six-layer OpenAI initialization gives 53.0/60.8 top-1 accuracy on Objaverse-LVIS/ScanObjectNN versus 55.2/66.3 for matching initialization. V3 also adds qualitative scene and concept-mixing results.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4.2 introduces a formal max-min similarity definition for selecting a shape that matches two normalized input embeddings. Existing contrastive-loss and attention equations are unchanged; no new theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the principal efficiency, generalization, and flexible-representation claims. V3's introduction additionally presents concept blending in the learned embedding space as a demonstrated capability, supported by Figure 2.

C2.justification: V3 explains matching initialization as facilitating fine-tuning and reducing potential overfitting, and discusses larger datasets enabling alternative backbones. It interprets the new retrieval examples as evidence of semantic and geometric concept organization while acknowledging imperfect visual matches. Earlier geometric-understanding and overfitting limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.5.1 newly specifies how attention visualizations are extracted, including the layer, token selection, patch dimensions, and overlay procedure. V3 also documents the alternate-initialization projection layer and retrieval protocols, and adds a direct code-repository link on the title page.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds explicit positioning against Gao et al.'s MixCon3D, emphasizing differences in point-cloud dependence and cross-view modeling. Additional citations cover robotics applications, DINO, image generation, and attention visualization; the broader related-work organization and positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: V3 rewrites the real-world dataset description, makes local grammatical edits, standardizes cross-references, and adds an appendix roadmap and explanatory subsections. The main narrative and section order remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: V3 adds four qualitative figures and an initialization table, expands Tables 2–4, and substantially restyles existing diagrams, plots, and retrieval panels. Changes include revised plot styling, rearranged panels, updated object renderings, and dotted ground-truth highlighting, beyond simple relocation or renumbering.

improvement.justification: Extending the existing single-view control, adding MixCon3D and the initialization test, and documenting visualization procedures strengthen validation and reproducibility. The gain is limited: original benchmark results and limitations persist, and the new distribution-shift and concept-mixing claims are supported primarily by selected qualitative examples.
